end_year.description: The year it ended; absent while it continues.

Affiliation.title: Affiliation

AffiliationKind.description: The kinds of affiliation an ORCID record holds.

turn_text.description: What was said in the turn.

turn_agent_id.description: For an agent turn, the agent that produced it.

turn_agent_version.description: For an agent turn, the version of the agent that produced it.

turn_invocation_id.description: For an agent turn, the invocation it came from.

ConversationTurn.title: ConversationTurn

DocumentationSummary.description: What one document a researcher attached to a project is, without its text: the conductor fills one per document into a Message so that the agent knows the project holds it (docs/specs/projects.md).

documentation_name.description: The file name the researcher attached the document under, without any folder.

documentation_digest.description: The SHA-256 of the document's UTF-8 text, by which the project keeps it.

documentation_media_type.description: The document's media type, text/plain or text/markdown.

documentation_size.description: The size of the document's UTF-8 text, in bytes.

documentation_added_at.description: When the document was added to the project.

DocumentationSummary.title: DocumentationSummary

ExternalIdentifier.description: An identifier from another scheme, as an ORCID record gives it: for a researcher, such as a Scopus Author ID; for a work, such as a DOI.

identifier_type.description: The scheme, in ORCID's words, such as doi or Scopus Author ID.

identifier_url.description: The identifier as a URL, where the record gives one.

ExternalIdentifier.title: ExternalIdentifier

inventory_digest.description: The inventory's dd-input-json-v1 hash, by which the project keeps it.

inventory_file_count.description: How many files the inventory lists.

inventory_tool.description: The command that made the inventory, such as dd-inventory.

inventory_tool_version.description: The version of the command that made the inventory.

inventory_limitations.description: What the inventory left out or could not do, such as files it skipped.

InventorySummary.title: InventorySummary

QuestionAnswer.description: The researcher's answer to one question of a reply, named by its question_key: the values of the options chosen, for a choice question, and the answer in their own words, for a text question or where a choice question allows it.

answered_key.description: The question_key of the question answered.

answer_values.description: The values of the options chosen, for a choice question; empty when the researcher answered in their own words, and always empty for a text question.

answer_words.description: The researcher's answer in their own words: the whole answer to a text question, or an answer given in place of an option where a choice question allows it.

QuestionAnswer.title: QuestionAnswer

ReplyAnswers.description: The researcher's answers to the questions the turn before asked, given together: one QuestionAnswer for each question answered, none for a question skipped. The app checks them against those questions before it sends the turn (docs/specs/orchestration.md).

answer_to.description: The invocation whose reply asked the questions.

given_answers.description: One answer for each question answered, in the order asked; at least one.

ReplyAnswers.title: ReplyAnswers

ResearcherFunding.description: One grant or award on an ORCID record, with its funder.

put_code.description: ORCID's identifier for the item within the record, by which a researcher chose to keep it.

funding_type.description: The kind of funding, in ORCID's words, such as grant or award.

funder_identifier.description: The funder's identifier, where ORCID gives one, such as a Crossref Funder ID.

funder_identifier_scheme.description: The scheme of funder_identifier, in ORCID's words, such as FUNDREF or ROR. Present exactly when funder_identifier is.

award_identifier.description: The grant number or award identifier, where the record gives one.

end_year.description: The year it ended; absent while it continues.

ResearcherFunding.title: ResearcherFunding

ResearcherLink.description: A web page the researcher lists on their ORCID record, such as a personal page.

link_title.description: The name the researcher gave the page.

ResearcherLink.title: ResearcherLink

ResearcherRecord.description: What one researcher in a project chose to keep from their public ORCID record: only the sections and items they ticked, in ORCID's own words, never edited by a person or a model. The conductor fills the project's records into a Message and a DraftRequest so that an agent can draft creators, affiliations, subjects and funding from them (docs/specs/projects.md). Email addresses are never kept, even public ones.

orcid_id.description: The researcher's ORCID iD, as its URL, such as https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097.

researcher_name.description: The researcher's name as their ORCID record gives it: the credit name, else the given and family names. Absent when they keep their name private or did not keep it.

other_names.description: Other names the researcher is known by, as their ORCID record lists them.

biography.description: The researcher's biography, as their ORCID record gives it.

keywords.description: The researcher's own keywords for their research, as their ORCID record lists them.

country.description: A country the researcher's ORCID record names, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

researcher_links.description: The web pages the researcher's ORCID record lists.

external_identifiers.description: The researcher's identifiers in other schemes, as their ORCID record lists them.

affiliations.description: The researcher's affiliations they kept, the current ones first.

works.description: The researcher's works they kept, the most recent first: at most 50 are offered, so that an agent's input stays bounded.

works_omitted.description: How many works the record held beyond the 50 offered. Absent when none were left out.

fundings.description: The researcher's grants and awards they kept, the current ones first.

record_retrieved_at.description: When the record was read from ORCID's public API.

record_source.description: The public API address the record was read from.

ResearcherRecord.title: ResearcherRecord

ResearcherWork.description: One work on an ORCID record, such as a journal article or a dataset.

put_code.description: ORCID's identifier for the item within the record, by which a researcher chose to keep it.

work_type.description: The work's type, in ORCID's words, such as journal-article or data-set.

publication_year.description: The year the work was published.

journal_title.description: Where the work was published, such as a journal's name.

work_identifiers.description: The work's identifiers, such as its DOI.

ResearcherWork.title: ResearcherWork

StepProgress.description: How far one step of the Blueprint's process flow has gone, as the project log shows it: started, done or skipped. A step the list leaves out is open (docs/specs/orchestration.md).
StepProgress.title: StepProgress

StepState.description: How far a process-flow step has gone; a step with none of these states is open.
StepState.title: StepState

TurnRole.description: Who spoke in a conversation turn.
TurnRole.title: TurnRole

description: One conversational turn addressed to an agent: the text of the turn and the conversation so far. The history is part of the input, so the input hash covers everything the agent saw. In a project that holds an inventory, the conductor adds what it is (docs/specs/projects.md); in any project, it adds the entry point chosen, the progress the project log shows and the project's title, if it has one (docs/specs/orchestration.md). It adds the researcher facts people in the project chose to keep from their public ORCID records (docs/specs/projects.md).

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

message_text.description: What the user said in this turn.

history.description: The earlier turns of the conversation, oldest first.

project_inventory.description: The inventory the conversation's project holds, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or its project holds no inventory.

reply_answers.description: The researcher's answers to the questions the previous turn asked, when they answered them in the form. message_text still carries the answers as prose.

project_entry.description: The Blueprint entry point (1, 2 or 3) the researcher chose for the conversation's project, the latest chosen. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project, or none was chosen.

project_progress.description: The process-flow steps the conversation's project log shows started, done or skipped, in flow order. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project. Derived from the log on every turn, never stored.

project_title.description: The conversation's project's latest title. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project, or the project has no title yet.

project_title_by_researcher.description: Whether a person gave the project its title, so that a model's would be refused; false while the project has no title. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project.

project_documentation.description: The documents the conversation's project holds, without their text, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or its project holds none.

project_entry_by_researcher.description: Whether the researcher chose the project's entry point, so that a model's would be refused; false when an orchestrator's model recorded it. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project, or no entry point was recorded.

project_researchers.description: The researcher facts the conversation's project holds, one record for each person who kept some, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or nobody in its project kept any.
